newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT - Telmex cut by JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Telmex cut by JP Morgan.

text.p: J.P. Morgan said on Thursday it lowered Mexican telephone company Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) to market performer from long-term buy.

-- "Telmex has performed strongly in recent weeks, up 23 percent to date -- recently surpassing our $38 target price and outpacing the 17 percent gain in the Mexican market," wrote J.P. Morgan Securities Inc analyst Simon Flannery.

-- "We do not believe there is significant near-term upside for the stock until we get much better visibility on the evolution of long-distance competition, which is unlikely to happen for at least six months."
-- Flannery wrote that he was also concerned about the impact of weak consumer demand, as fourth quarter earnings showed a sharp deterioration in calling volumes in December.

-- J.P. Morgan says it expects Telmex to lose an average of 20 percent of its long-distance market share this year, with an average loss reaching some 33 percent in 1998. Domestic long-distance pricing is likely to fall by 30 percent in 1997, with additional declines in international and settlements rates.
-- "We are lowering our earnings estimates to reflect more conservative market share, pricing and line growth assumptions," the company wrote.
-- "We recognize that Telmex is in a good position to withstand competition, with a stellar financial profile, a modern network, and a strong management team," it said.
-- Telmex L shares fell 0.12 peso to 15.60 pesos, while its ADRs were off 1/2 at 40-1/4.
